questions.event_title: Mayor Combo: Taipei and New Taipei
questions.question: Will the DPP win the Taipei and New Taipei mayoral elections?
questions.rules:
This market will resolve according to the outcome of the Taipei and New Taipei mayoral elections that are currently scheduled for November 28, 2026.

A candidate will be considered to represent a party by their ballot-listed affiliation or if they are the nominee of that party. Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “KMT” or “DPP” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

If the results of one of these elections are not conclusively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or if an independent or third-party candidate wins one of these elections, this market will resolve to "Other".

For purposes of this market, a "sweep" is when a party wins all races.

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Taiwanese government, specifically the Central Election Commission (https://db.cec.gov.tw/).

questions.question: Will the Fear & Greed Index be 24 or below on November 27?
questions.rules:
This market will resolve according to the CNN Fear & Greed Index closing value for November 27, 2026.

The closing value is the value shown for November 27, 2026 in the "Timeline" tab (the historical chart) of the Fear & Greed Index at https://www.cnn.com/markets/fear-and-greed at the time CNN first shows a value for the next trading day after November 27, 2026. Changes CNN makes to the value for November 27, 2026 after that time are not considered, unless the value shown at that time was clearly erroneous, in which case the correction paragraph below applies. Values shown for November 27, 2026 before then, while the index is still updating, and the separate previous-close and other summary figures CNN displays, are not used. If the value is shown with decimals, the decimals are dropped (e.g., 24.9 counts as 24).

The brackets are whole-number ranges that include both numbers shown (e.g., "25–34" includes 25 and 34). They follow CNN's own rating zones: 0–24 Extreme Fear; 25–44 Fear; 45–55 Neutral; 56–75 Greed; 76–100 Extreme Greed.

If CNN has not shown a value for the next trading day within seven (7) calendar days after November 27, 2026, the value shown for November 27, 2026 at the end of that period will be used. If CNN shows no value for November 27, 2026 within that period, this market will resolve according to the value for November 27, 2026 published by a successor index from CNN under the same or a substantially similar name, if one exists. Otherwise, this market will resolve to the "45–55" bracket.

The resolution source for this market is CNN's Fear & Greed Index, available at https://www.cnn.com/markets/fear-and-greed.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

questions.question: Will Greens win the third-most seats in the next Victorian state election?
questions.rules:
The 2026 Victorian state election is currently scheduled to be held on 28 November 2026 to elect members of the 61st Parliament of Victoria.

This market will resolve to "Yes" according to which party or coalition wins the third-most seats in the Legislative Assembly (Victoria's lower house) as a result of the next Victorian state election.

If the results of this election are not known definitively by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

Liberal–National refers to the Liberal–National Coalition. Liberal–National will include all seats won by both the Liberal Party and the Nationals, regardless of their parliamentary coalition behaviour, and its first-preference vote total will include the votes received by both parties.

Parties and coalitions will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid first-preference votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If they remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the party or coalition that occupies the third-highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Victorian government, specifically the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC) (https://www.vec.vic.gov.au/).

questions.event_title: Spain General Election: PSOE % of vote?
questions.question: Will PSOE receive 30% or more of the vote in the 2026 Spanish general election?
questions.rules:
Legislative elections to elect the 350 members of the Congress of Deputies of Spain are scheduled to take place on November 29, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the percentage of the valid votes cast in the election to the Congress of Deputies of Spain received by the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE).

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, this market will resolve to the higher bracket.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by November 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The vote share will be calculated as the total number of valid votes received by the lists attributed to PSOE divided by the total number of valid votes cast, as reported in the official results.

Seats and votes will be attributed according to the electoral list on which they were obtained, as reported in the official results, regardless of the party membership of individual candidates. Lists will be attributed as follows:

PSOE: lists of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party, including the Partit dels Socialistes de Catalunya (PSC) lists in Catalonia.

PP: lists of the People's Party, including the joint UPN–PP list in Navarre.

Broad Front (FA): all Broad Front lists, including Catalunya en Comú in Catalonia, Compromís–Valencian Front in the Valencian Community, and Canarian People’s Unity (UPC) in the Canary Islands.

ERC: Republican Left of Catalonia lists, including the joint ERC–Podem lists in Catalonia.

Podemos: only lists presented by Podemos on its own.

CCa: Canarian Coalition lists, including the joint CCa–1º CAN lists in the Canary Islands.

Any other list will be attributed to the party or coalition that presents it, as named in the official proclamation of candidacies.

Electoral cooperation, endorsements, coalition agreements, or subsequent changes in party affiliation or parliamentary-group membership will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Spanish Ministry of the Interior (https://infoelectoral.interior.gob.es/).
